title: Unified Framework for Bidirectional and Cyclic Teleportation under Noise
authors: Soubhik De, Vedhanayagi R, Basherrudin Mahmud Ahmed A, Alok Sharan
abstract: Quantum teleportation has evolved from single-qubit, unidirectional communication to multi-qubit and multidirectional protocols. However, most existing schemes rely on protocol-specific entangled resources, motivating the development of universal quantum channels capable of supporting multiple communication tasks simultaneously. In this work, we demonstrate that a single twelve-qubit entangled channel exhibits such versatility by enabling the bidirectional teleportation of arbitrary three-qubit states and the cyclic teleportation of arbitrary two-qubit states through local Bell-state measurements and single-qubit operations. Both protocols are further generalized to multi-qubit and multi-party configurations, establishing the scalability of the proposed framework. To assess its practical applicability, the protocols are analyzed under amplitude-damping, phase-damping, bit-flip, phase-flip, and depolarizing noise channels by plotting the teleportation fidelity as a function of both the input-state parameters and noise strength. The analysis reveals distinct noise sensitivities, with the bidirectional protocol remaining perfectly faithful under bit-flip noise for all input states and noise strengths, while the cyclic protocol is consistently more vulnerable to environmental disturbances. The proposed schemes achieve an intrinsic efficiency of $25\%$, which is compared with several existing protocols. The framework therefore provides a scalable and resource-efficient approach to unified quantum communication in realistic noisy quantum networks.
summary: This paper presents a unified framework using a single twelve-qubit entangled resource to achieve both bidirectional and cyclic quantum teleportation. The authors demonstrate the protocols' scalability and analyze their performance under various noise models, showing that the bidirectional scheme is remarkably robust against bit-flip errors.
main_problem: The work aims to develop a unified quantum communication framework capable of supporting both bidirectional and cyclic teleportation using a single, shared entangled resource.
main_result: A twelve-qubit entangled channel was shown to enable the bidirectional teleportation of three-qubit states and cyclic teleportation of two-qubit states. The protocol maintains perfect fidelity under bit-flip noise for the bidirectional case while achieving an intrinsic efficiency of 25%.
method: The authors utilize local Bell-state measurements (BSM) on a pre-established multi-qubit entangled channel and apply subsequent single-qubit operations to reconstruct the unknown quantum state.
model_or_system: The core model is a twelve-qubit entangled resource ($\vert G_{12} angle$) used to facilitate communication between multiple parties. The protocols are analyzed by subjecting them to various noise channels, including amplitude-damping and depolarizing noise.
key_observables: Teleportation Fidelity (as a function of input state parameters and noise strength $p$), intrinsic efficiency, and the final collapsed quantum state after measurements.
important_parameters: Noise strengths ($p$) for various channels (amplitude-damping, bit-flip, etc.), and the number of qubits involved in the teleportation tasks (3-qubit states, 2-qubit cycles).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to perform local Bell-state measurements and single-qubit operations on the shared entangled resource.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates bidirectional teleportation ($A \leftrightarrow B \leftrightarrow C$), and Figure 2 plots the fidelity of both bidirectional and cyclic protocols against the noise parameter $p$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem, then details the construction of the twelve-qubit channel. It proceeds to derive the mathematical steps for the three-qubit bidirectional and cyclic teleportation protocols using BSMs. Finally, it analyzes the performance of these schemes under various noise models.
why_interesting: The rigorous analysis of multi-party quantum communication channels under realistic noise conditions is highly relevant for developing robust quantum networks and understanding decoherence effects in complex quantum information tasks.
